extracted.intended_audience: New Yorker readers and puzzle players (casual and regular)
extracted.subtask_description: Browsing and playing the New Yorker’s assortment of puzzles and games (daily crossword, mini, cryptic crosswords, Shuffalo, Laugh Lines, Name Drop, and themed packs). The page describes each game's core mechanic or experience and links to how-to/play materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shuffalo core mechanic
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you make a longer word with each new letter?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a daily anagramming challenge with a twist; implied design rule: each move/step should produce a longer valid word as letters are added. Presented as a daily game (e.g., Shuffalo: Sunday, May 10, 2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Crossword — difficulty and theme
rubrics_metrics.description: A puzzle that ranges in difficulty, with the occasional theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/evaluation guidance: puzzles should vary in difficulty to appeal to a range of solvers and sometimes center on a theme. Multiple daily puzzles are published (dates listed).

rubrics_metrics.name: The Mini (Mini Crossword) — brevity and quick diversion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Mini: A bite-size crossword, for a quick diversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design constraint: short form, meant for quick play rather than extended solving sessions. Implied expectation: concise grid and fast clues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laugh Lines — cartoon-dating mechanic
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you guess when these New Yorker cartoons were originally published?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Game focuses on historical/caption context of cartoons; published as a weekly challenge (Laugh Lines No. 70, 69, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Name Drop — identify person from limited clues
rubrics_metrics.description: Can you guess the notable person in six clues or fewer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pack-based quiz format (Name Drop Packs) with themed sets (e.g., Oscar winners, music legends). Design/evaluation principle: provide up to six progressive clues to identify an individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptic Crossword — wily wordplay
rubrics_metrics.description: The Cryptic Crossword: A puzzle for lovers of wily wordplay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/evaluation principle: clues rely on cryptic clue conventions and playful, tricky wordplay aimed at experienced solvers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginner-Friendly Cryptic — accessibility via hints
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginner-Friendly Cryptic No. 1: We’ve added some hints and explainers to make this puzzle a little less cryptic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility guideline: include hints and explainers for cryptic-style puzzles when targeting novices; supports learning cryptic conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rough Copy variant — intentionally loose clues
rubrics_metrics.description: The Crossword: Rough Copy — A puzzle with a few clues loose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variant-format principle: publish intentionally imperfect/quirky puzzles (e.g., 'rough copy') that break or loosen some usual constraints for novelty or theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta/hidden-caption puzzle mechanic
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Flurry: Solve the clues to reveal a cartoon caption hidden in the snow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design pattern: clues map to a concealed message or caption; solver activity reveals hidden text rather than (or in addition to) filling a standard grid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game packaging: themed packs and editorial curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Name Drop Pack and other themed packs (e.g., 'And the Oscar Goes To...', 'Music Legends', 'Make Me Laugh')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial guideline: group puzzles/quizzes into themed packs to create cohesive experiences and replayable collections for topical interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred delivery medium
rubrics_metrics.description: For the best experience, solve in the New Yorker app.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage recommendation: the publisher advises using the app for optimal interaction with puzzles and games; implies design/testing should target the app experience.
